arabic: نَظَّمَ الْمُوَظَّفُ إِجْرَاءَ تَوْفِيرِ الْعِلَاجِ الْحَدِيثِ مِنْ أَجْلِ شِفَاءِ الْمَرِيضِ.
english: The employee organized the procedure for providing modern treatment to help the patient recover.
reason: Grammatical and coherent administrative wording; the translation preserves the purpose of providing treatment.

arabic: صَاحِبُ الْمَخْبَزِ يَمْتَلِكُ نِصْفَ هَذِهِ الْعِمَارَةِ، وَيَعْتَبِرُهَا ثَرْوَةً لَهُ وَلِابْنِهِ.
english: The bakery owner owns half of this building and considers it wealth for himself and his son.
reason: A plausible statement about property ownership and family wealth, accurately translated.

arabic: فِي هَذَا الدَّلِيلِ مَقَاسُ كُلِّ طَقْمٍ وَحَجْمُهُ، مِنْ أَجْلِ شِرَائِهِ.
english: This guide gives the size and dimensions of each set to help with purchasing it.
reason: A complete nominal sentence describing information in a purchasing guide; the English reasonably conveys the measurements.

arabic: تَعِبَ الرَّجُلُ مِنَ التَّزَلُّجِ، وَدَامَتْ مُعَانَاتُهُ مِنَ الْأَلَمِ ثَلَاثِينَ دَقِيقَةً.
english: The man became tired from skiing, and his pain lasted thirty minutes.
reason: A plausible account of fatigue and pain after skiing; the translation preserves the meaning.

arabic: شَهَادَةُ الْمُوَظَّفِ تَعْكِسُ نَزَاهَتَهُ، لَكِنَّهُ الْآنَ فِي السِّجْنِ بِسَبَبِهَا.
english: The employee’s testimony reflects his integrity, but he is now in prison because of it.
reason: Coherent: honest testimony could lead to imprisonment. The translation is accurate.

arabic: أَفَلَ الْهِلَالُ وَأَظْلَمَ الْمَيْدَانُ، فَأَضَاءَ الرَّجُلُ شَمْعَةً وَتَوَهَّجَ ضِيَاؤُهَا.
english: The crescent moon set and the square grew dark, so the man lit a candle, and its light glowed.
reason: Grammatical, plausible narrative language with an accurate translation.

arabic: شَمِلَ فَصْلُ الْأَبْجَدِيَّةِ أَمْثِلَةً مُتَعَدِّدَةً، ثُمَّ تَلَاهُ فَصْلٌ فِي التَّرْجَمَةِ.
english: The chapter on the alphabet included several examples, followed by a chapter on translation.
reason: A natural description of successive book chapters, accurately translated.

arabic: تَصَوَّرَ الْوَلَدُ فَرَاشَةً مُنْفَرِدَةً عَلَى الْعُشْبِ، ثُمَّ رَسَمَهَا عَلَى وَرَقَةٍ.
english: The boy imagined a lone butterfly on the grass, then drew it on a sheet of paper.
reason: A coherent scene of imagining and drawing a butterfly; the translation is accurate.

arabic: الْوَلَدُ اِسْتَحْيَا مِنْ قُبْلَةِ جَدَّتِهِ أَمَامَ الطُّلَّابِ، فَمَسَحَ شَفَتَهُ بِثَوْبِهِ.
english: The boy was embarrassed by his grandmother’s kiss in front of the students, so he wiped his lip with his garment.
reason: A plausible reaction by an embarrassed child; the English accurately preserves the details.

arabic: أَدِرْ هَذَا الْقَضِيبَ بِهَذِهِ الْأَدَاةِ مِنْ أَجْلِ إِيقَافِ الْآلَةِ.
english: Turn this rod with this tool to stop the machine.
reason: A grammatical and plausible mechanical instruction, accurately translated.

arabic: هَلْ شَرَطَ صَاحِبُ الْمَطْعَمِ حَجْزًا مُسْبَقًا لِتَحْضِيرِ الْمَنْدِي غَدًا؟
english: Did the restaurant owner require an advance booking to prepare mandi tomorrow?
reason: The verb شَرَطَ can mean to stipulate or require; the booking question is coherent and accurately translated.

arabic: لَمْ يَصُمْ جَدِّي هَذَا الْعَامَ، فَقَدْ نَحُلَ وَشَحَبَ وَجْهُهُ وَسَعَلَ.
english: My grandfather did not fast this year, as he had grown thin, his face had become pale, and he had been coughing.
reason: Grammatical and plausible; the English appropriately expresses the preceding illness as the reason for not fasting.

arabic: اِسْتَعَانَ الْمُصَوِّرُ بِالْمِعْمَارِ فِي قِيَاسِ ارْتِفَاعِ هَذَا الْمَبْنَى فِي الصَّبَاحِ.
english: The photographer sought the architect’s help in measuring this building’s height in the morning.
reason: Grammatical and plausible; المعمار can mean architect, and the translation is accurate.

arabic: النَّادِلُ خَلَطَ الْخَرْدَلَ بِالْفُولِ الْمَالِحِ فِي هَذَا الْكُوبِ فَقَطْ.
english: The waiter mixed mustard into the salty fava beans in this cup only.
reason: A plausible food-preparation statement, with correct grammar and an accurate translation.

arabic: هَذِهِ الْمُحَاضَرَةُ الْمَجَّانِيَّةُ فِي تَصْنِيفِ الْمَادَّةِ مُمْتِعَةٌ جِدًّا لِكُلِّ طَالِبٍ.
english: This free lecture on classifying matter is very enjoyable for every student.
reason: A natural educational statement; the translation accurately conveys the meaning.

arabic: فِي الْمَقَرِّ الْإِدَارِيِّ، تَذَمَّرَتْ مَجْمُوعَةٌ مِنَ الطُّلَّابِ الْأَجَانِبِ مِنْ صُعُوبَةِ الِامْتِحَانِ.
english: At the administrative headquarters, a group of foreign students complained about the exam’s difficulty.
reason: Correct grammar and a coherent situation; the English matches the Arabic.

arabic: مَا دَاعِي اعْتِرَاضِ الرِّئَاسَةِ عَلَى جَلْبِ حَاسُوبٍ لِهَذَا الْقِسْمِ؟
english: Why does the leadership object to bringing a computer to this department?
reason: A natural question about an administrative objection, translated accurately.

arabic: أَحْمَدُ مَارَسَ النُّطْقَ بِجِدٍّ، ثُمَّ أَعَادَ هَذَا الْقَوْلَ ثَلَاثَ مَرَّاتٍ.
english: Ahmad practiced pronunciation diligently, then repeated this saying three times.
reason: The phrasing مارس النطق is somewhat less idiomatic than تدرّب على النطق, but understandable and plausible. The translation is accurate.

arabic: عَجِبَ الطَّالِبُ مِنْ ذَنَبِ الطَّاوُوسِ الَّذِي دَارَ هُنَا فِي الصَّبَاحِ.
english: The student marveled at the tail of the peacock that turned around here in the morning.
reason: Grammatical and plausible; the relative clause can describe the peacock, as translated.

arabic: كُلَّ صَبَاحٍ، أَدْرُسُ طَبِيعَةَ النِّرْوَيْجِ، وَمُحْتَوَى هَذَا الْكِتَابِ مُفِيدٌ.
english: Every morning, I study Norway’s natural environment, and this book’s content is useful.
reason: A coherent learner-level statement about studying Norway’s natural environment; accurately translated.

arabic: الْحَقِيبَةُ الَّتِي عَبَّأَهَا الْجَارُ بِحَطَبِ الزَّانِ ثَقِيلَةٌ، وَالْفَأْسُ ثَقِيلَةٌ أَيْضًا.
english: The bag that the neighbor filled with beech firewood is heavy, and the axe is heavy too.
reason: A plausible description with correct agreement, including the feminine الفأس. The translation is accurate.

arabic: لَمْ يُنْهِ الْمُغَنِّي التَّرْنِيمَةَ، وَصَمَتَ لِأَنَّ الْتِهَابَ الْحَنْجَرَةِ مُتْعِبٌ جِدًّا.
english: The singer did not finish the hymn and fell silent because the throat inflammation was very exhausting.
reason: A coherent explanation for stopping singing, with correct grammar and an accurate translation.

arabic: رُبَّمَا وَقَعَ شِهَابٌ فِي الْغَابَةِ، فَالذُّعْرُ مُنْتَشِرٌ هُنَا الْآنَ.
english: Perhaps a meteor fell in the forest, as fear is widespread here now.
reason: A plausible speculative explanation for widespread fear; the translation preserves the meaning.

arabic: إِنَّ ذِكْرَى إِيَابِ ابْنِهَا مُؤَثِّرَةٌ جِدًّا، وَقَدْ بَاحَتْ بِهَا لِجَارَتِهَا.
english: The memory of her son’s return is very moving, and she has confided it to her neighbor.
reason: Formal but plausible phrasing about sharing a moving memory; the translation is accurate.

arabic: أَضَافَ الطَّالِبُ حَفْنَةً مِنَ السُّكَّرِ إِلَى خَلِيطِ الزُّبْدَةِ وَالزَّيْتِ.
english: The student added a handful of sugar to the butter and oil mixture.
reason: Grammatical, plausible cooking scene; the translation is accurate.

arabic: الْمُتَخَصِّصُ السُّورِيُّ يَشْتَغِلُ فِي مَجَالِ الصَّوْتِيَّاتِ، وَهُوَ مَجَالٌ مُعَقَّدٌ جِدًّا.
english: The Syrian specialist works in phonetics, which is a very complex field.
reason: Natural description of a specialist's field; phonetics is an accurate rendering here.

arabic: هَلْ وَجَدْتَ فِي الدُّرْجِ رِبْطَةً مُلَائِمَةً لِهَذِهِ الْبِذْلَةِ الْحَمْرَاءِ؟
english: Did you find a suitable tie for this red suit in the drawer?
reason: A plausible question about finding a matching tie; the translation is accurate.

arabic: بِسُرُورٍ، شَاهَدَ الْجَارُ عَوْدَةَ السِّنْجَابِ الَّذِي أَنْقَذَهُ مِنَ الشَّبَكَةِ.
english: The neighbor watched with delight as the squirrel he had rescued from the net returned.
reason: Coherent account of a rescued squirrel returning; the translation preserves the meaning.

arabic: النَّمِرُ قَفَزَ عَلَى الْحَارِسِ بِضَرَاوَةٍ، لَكِنَّ الْحَارِسَ نَجَا بِحِيلَةٍ.
english: The tiger leaped fiercely at the guard, but the guard escaped using a trick.
reason: Grammatical and plausible in a narrative; the translation is accurate.

arabic: فِي الْجَرَاجِ، مَنَعَ الْمُهَنْدِسُ عَبَثَ الْغُلَامِ بِعَجَلَةِ الْعَرَبَةِ الْقَدِيمَةِ.
english: In the garage, the engineer stopped the boy from tampering with the old cart's wheel.
reason: A coherent scene involving a boy tampering with a wheel; accurately translated.

arabic: لَمْ يَتَجَاهَلِ الطَّالِبُ شُحُوبَ جَارِهِ، فَحَمَلَهُ إِلَى عِيَادَةٍ لِرِعَايَتِهِ.
english: The student did not ignore his neighbor's pallor, so he carried him to a clinic for care.
reason: A plausible response to a neighbor appearing unwell; grammar and translation are correct.

arabic: أَحْمَدُ سَخِرَ مِنْ لِحْيَةِ جَارِهِ، فَتَوَلَّدَ صِرَاعٌ فِي الْمُنْتَدَى الْإِلِكْتُرُونِيِّ.
english: Ahmed mocked his neighbor's beard, which sparked a conflict in the online forum.
reason: A plausible online dispute prompted by mockery; the translation is accurate.

arabic: كَثْرَةُ ظُهُورِ هَذَا الْمَغْرُورِ فِي الْمُسَلْسَلِ مُمِلَّةٌ جِدًّا لِي.
english: This arrogant man's frequent appearances in the series are very boring to me.
reason: A natural expression of annoyance at someone's repeated appearances; accurately translated.

arabic: أَثْنَاءَ الصِّيَامِ، ضَعُفَتْ عَضَلَةُ فَخِذِهِ، فَلَمْ يَسْتَمِرَّ فِي السِّبَاحَةِ.
english: While fasting, his thigh muscle weakened, so he did not continue swimming.
reason: A plausible account of muscle weakness interrupting swimming during fasting; accurately translated.

arabic: أَطْعِمِ الْعِجْلَ هَذَا الْقَمْحَ الرَّطْبَ مِنَ الْكِيسِ الَّذِي عَلَى الْعَرَبَةِ.
english: Feed the calf this moist wheat from the bag on the cart.
reason: A grammatical, coherent feeding instruction; the translation is accurate.

arabic: لِمَ لَمْ تَدْعَمِ الْجِهَةُ هَذِهِ التَّجْرِبَةَ الْفَرِيدَةَ فِي اسْتِضَافَةِ الزَّائِرِينَ؟
english: Why didn't the organization support this unique experiment in hosting visitors?

arabic: الطَّحَّانُ الصَّبُورُ كَنَسَ الْمَطْحَنَةَ، ثُمَّ أَغْلَقَ الْبَوَّابَةَ فِي ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمِ.
english: The patient miller swept the mill, then closed the gate that day.
reason: Grammatical, plausible, and accurately translated.

arabic: هَلْ حَرَّكَ الطَّبَّاخُ الْبَامْيَا وَالْبَهَارَ فِي هَذِهِ الزَّبْدِيَّةِ النُّحَاسِيَّةِ؟
english: Did the cook stir the okra and spices in this copper bowl?
reason: A plausible cooking question. البهار can refer collectively to spices or seasoning.

arabic: أَنَا جَوْعَانُ، لَكِنَّنِي أُرِيدُ سَنْدَوِيتْشِي الْمُفَضَّلَ فَقَطْ، لَا كَرُوَاسُونًا وَلَا هَمْبَرْجَرًا.
english: I'm hungry, but I only want my favorite sandwich, no croissant or hamburger.
reason: Natural expression of a food preference, accurately translated.

arabic: الْهَمْسْتَرُ الْمَنْفُوشُ مُولَعٌ بِالْإِجَّاصِ، وَهُوَ الْآنَ فِي هَذَا الرُّكْنِ.
english: The fluffy hamster loves pears, and he is in this corner now.
reason: A coherent description of a pet; the translation preserves the meaning.

arabic: تَحَرَّكَتْ سُلَحْفَاةٌ فِي التَّيَّارِ الضَّحْلِ، بَعِيدًا عَنْ هَذِهِ الدَّوَّامَةِ الْعَنِيفَةِ.
english: A turtle moved in the shallow current, far from this violent whirlpool.
reason: A plausible description of a turtle moving through shallow water; the translation is accurate.

arabic: فَرَدَ الرَّجُلُ الْجَلَّابِيَّةَ عَلَى الْجِينْزِ، ثُمَّ لَاحَظَ تَجْعِيدَةً فِيهَا.
english: The man spread the traditional robe over the jeans, then noticed a wrinkle in it.
reason: Spreading one garment over another is plausible, and the translation matches.

arabic: تَوَقَّعْتُ لُغْزًا فِي هَذِهِ الْأُسْطُورَةِ، لَكِنَّ سُطُورَهَا لَغْوٌ بِلَا تَشْوِيقٍ.
english: I expected a riddle in this legend, but its lines are nonsense without suspense.
reason: A coherent literary criticism, with an accurate English translation.

arabic: لَمْ يُدَافِعِ الْأَمِيرُ عَنْ رَعِيَّتِهِ مِنَ الْقَمْعِ وَتَقْيِيدِ الْحُرِّيَّةِ.
english: The prince did not defend his subjects against repression and restrictions on freedom.
reason: Grammatical and meaningful. The kasra in يُدَافِعِ appropriately avoids consecutive vowelless consonants in connected speech.

arabic: أَصْغَيْتُ إِلَى جَدَّتِي الْمُؤَنِّبَةِ بِخَجَلٍ، لَا بِعِنَادٍ وَلَا بِلَامُبَالَاةٍ.
english: I listened to my scolding grandmother with shame, without stubbornness or indifference.
reason: A plausible reaction to a grandmother's scolding. خجل can convey shame or embarrassment here.

arabic: أَحَبَّتْ جَدَّتِي حَلَاوَةَ الْعِرْقْسُوسِ، لَكِنَّهَا طَلَبَتْ نَعْنَاعًا مَغْلِيًّا فَقَطْ.
english: My grandmother liked the sweetness of licorice, but she only ordered boiled mint.
reason: A coherent contrast between enjoying licorice's sweetness and ordering mint; the translation matches.

arabic: قَادَ الْقَانِصُ أَصْحَابَهُ إِلَى الْجَبَلِ بِمَشَقَّةٍ فِي عَاصِفَةٍ فَظِيعَةٍ.
english: The hunter led his friends to the mountain with difficulty in a terrible storm.
reason: A plausible account of a difficult journey, accurately translated.

arabic: غَمَرَتِ الْغِبْطَةُ الطَّبَّاخَ، فَقَدْ تَنَاوَلَ أَصْحَابُهُ الْمَنْسَفَ وَالْمُقَبِّلَاتِ بِحَمَاسٍ.
english: Joy filled the cook, for his friends had eaten the mansaf and appetizers enthusiastically.
reason: The cook's happiness at his friends' enthusiastic eating is coherent and accurately translated.

arabic: تَعِبَ الرَّجُلُ مِنْ مُعَانَاةِ السِّجْنِ، وَدَامَ حُزْنُهُ فِي قَلْبِهِ زَمَانًا.
english: The man grew tired of the suffering of prison, and the sadness in his heart lasted a long time.
reason: Grammatical, coherent literary phrasing; the translation preserves the meaning.

arabic: لَمْ يُنَاسِبْ هَذَا الطَّقْمُ مَقَاسَ الوَلَدِ، فَغَيَّظَهُ شِرَاؤُهُ.
english: This set did not suit the boy's size, so buying it made him angry.
reason: A plausible description of frustration over an ill-fitting purchase; accurately translated.

arabic: أَضَاءَ الهِلَالُ المَدِينَةَ، وَكَانَتِ الصَّائِمَاتُ فِي مِزَاجٍ رَائِعٍ.
english: The crescent lit up the city, and the fasting women were in a wonderful mood.
reason: The crescent illuminating the city is acceptable poetic imagery. The translation is accurate.

arabic: يَاتُرَى مَا حَجْمُ ثَرْوَةِ صَاحِبِ العِمَارَةِ، وَهَلِ امْتَلَكَهَا بِنَزَاهَةٍ؟
english: I wonder how large the wealth of the building's owner is, and did he come to own it with integrity?
reason: A plausible question about someone's wealth and how honestly it was acquired; accurately translated.

arabic: لَعَلَّ الدَّلِيلَ الَّذِي قَدِمَ مَعَنَا يَهْدِي الوَفْدَ إِلَى المَطْعَمِ.
english: Perhaps the guide who came with us will lead the delegation to the restaurant.
reason: Natural, grammatical Arabic with an accurate translation.

arabic: هَاجَرَ نِصْفُ الصِّرْبِ إِلَى المَدِينَةِ بِسَبَبِ أَزْمَةٍ أَهْلِيَّةٍ.
english: Half of the Serbs emigrated to the city because of a civil crisis.
reason: A coherent statement about migration among a contextually understood Serbian population; accurately translated.

arabic: بَعْدَ غَسْلِ الوَجْهِ، مَسَحَ الوَلَدُ حَاجِبَهُ، لَكِنَّ اللَّزْقَةَ كَانَتْ مُلْتَصِقَةً بِهِ.
english: After washing his face, the boy wiped his eyebrow, but the plaster was still stuck to it.
reason: A plausible scene involving an adhesive plaster on an eyebrow. 'Still' is reasonably implied by the contrast.

arabic: اِسْتَحْيَا الوَلَدُ مِنْ قُبْلَةِ الجَدَّةِ فَهَمَسَ لَهَا وَلَمْ يَكُنْ زَعْلَانَ.
english: The boy felt shy at his grandmother's kiss, so he whispered to her and was not upset.
reason: A plausible description of a shy child's reaction. The informal زعلان is acceptable, and the translation matches.

arabic: حَرَثَ الجَدُّ المَزْرَعَةَ بَاكِرًا ثُمَّ سَنَا العُشْبَ وَالتُّوتَ.
english: Grandfather plowed the farm early, then watered the grass and the mulberries.
reason: سنا is a rare but attested verb meaning to water; التوت can refer to mulberry plants. See the [Arabic Language Academy dictionary](https://www.arabicacademy.gov.eg/ar/search_engine/roots/س%20ن%20و%20–%20ي).

arabic: عَاقَبَ المَأْمُورُ الرَّجُلَ بِالحَبْسِ بَعْدَ إِيقَافِهِ، فَكَانَ الإِجْرَاءُ بَاتًّا.
english: The officer punished the man with confinement after stopping him, and the procedure was definitive.
reason: Somewhat stiff administrative phrasing, but grammatical and plausible; باتًّا conveys finality, matching 'definitive.'

arabic: هَلْ شَمِلَ الاِخْتِبَارُ المُسْبَقُ فِي هَذَا الفَصْلِ الأَبْجَدِيَّةَ وَالأَدَبَ الحَدِيثَ؟
english: Did the preliminary test in this class include the alphabet and modern literature?
reason: A preliminary assessment can cover both basic literacy and literature. The question is grammatical and accurately translated.

arabic: نَظَّمَ المُوَظَّفُ نَوْبَاتٍ مُتَعَدِّدَةً فِي المَطْعَمِ لِتَوْفِيرِ الوَقْتِ.
english: The employee organized multiple shifts in the restaurant in order to save time.

arabic: رَغِبَ المُصَوِّرُ فِي زِيَارَةِ نِرْوَيج لِأَنَّ طَبِيعَتَهَا مُمْتِعَةٌ جِدًّا.
english: The photographer wanted to visit Norway because its nature is very enjoyable.
reason: Grammatical and plausible; the translation preserves the meaning.

arabic: صَاحَ النَّادِلُ مِنَ الذُّعْرِ فَوَقَعَ الظَّرْفُ مِنْهُ ثُمَّ صَمَتَ.
english: The waiter shouted in terror, so the container fell from him, and then he fell silent.
reason: A coherent scene. ظَرْف can mean a container, although an envelope is the more familiar meaning.

arabic: بِالفَاسِ قَلَعَ العَبْدُ الزَّانَ، ثُمَّ أَخَذَ الحَطَبَ وَالعُودَ إِلَى المَبْنَى.
english: With the axe the servant uprooted the beech tree, then took the firewood and the timber to the building.
reason: The standard spelling for axe is الفَأْس. العَبْد means slave, rather than simply servant; العُود here is a stick or piece of wood, not necessarily timber.

arabic: الطَّبَّاعَةُ هُنَا فِي مَقَرِّ القِسْمِ الإِدَارِيِّ مَجَّانِيَّةٌ لِلْمَجْمُوعَةِ فَقَطْ.
english: The printer here at the administrative department's headquarters is free for the group only.
reason: الطَّبَّاعَة does not mean the printer as a machine; that is الطَّابِعَة. If printing is intended, use الطِّبَاعَة and translate it as printing.

arabic: تَذَمَّرَ الطِّفْلُ الآنَ لِأَنَّ فِي حَنْجَرَتِهِ خَدَرًا وَلُعَابُهُ مَالِحٌ.
english: The child is complaining now because there is numbness in his throat and his saliva is salty.
reason: A plausible description of a child's symptoms. With الآن, the translation reasonably conveys the immediate complaint.

arabic: اِسْتَعَانَ الجَارُ بِمِقَصٍّ وَمُشْطٍ، ثُمَّ اسْتَحَمَّ وَارْتَدَى رِدَاءً نَظِيفًا.
english: The neighbor used scissors and a comb, then bathed and put on a clean robe.
reason: A plausible grooming sequence, with an accurate translation.

arabic: أَنْهَى المِعْمَارُ هَذَا الصَّرْحَ الحَضَارِيَّ، وَاسْتَحَقَّ رِئَاسَةَ القِسْمِ أَيْضًا.
english: The architect finished this civilized edifice, and he also deserved the leadership of the department.
reason: Grammatical and plausible. 'Cultural edifice' would be more idiomatic English than 'civilized edifice.'

arabic: نَوَّعَتِ الهِنْدُ صِنَاعَتَهَا، وَتَمَّ جَلْبُ مِلْيُونِ حَاسُوبٍ إِلَيْهَا فِي أُسْبُوعٍ.
english: India diversified its industry, and a million computers were brought to it in a week.
reason: A coherent statement about industry and computer imports; the translation is accurate.

arabic: فِي صَبَاحٍ مُشْمِسٍ دَفَّ الطَّاوُوسُ وَتَرَقْرَقَ ذَنَبُهُ فِي الفِرْدَوْسِ.
english: On a sunny morning the peacock flapped its wings and its tail shimmered in the paradise.
reason: Plausible poetic imagery. دَفَّ can describe a bird's wing movement, and ترقرق can convey shimmering.

arabic: رُبَّمَا خَفِيَ الشِّهَابُ عَنْ بَصَرِ المُتَجَوِّلِ فِي الظُّلْمَةِ فَعَجِبَ.
english: Perhaps the meteor was hidden from the wanderer's sight in the darkness, and he wondered.
reason: Grammatical and plausible; عَجِبَ conveys wondering or being astonished.

arabic: طَحَنَ الجَارُ الخَرْدَلَ وَخَلَطَهُ بِالثُّومِ ثُمَّ عَبَأَهُ فِي كُوبٍ.
english: The neighbor ground the mustard, mixed it with garlic, and then filled a cup with it.
reason: A coherent food preparation scene, accurately translated.

arabic: لَمْ يَكُنْ هُنَاكَ اعْتِرَاضٌ عَلَى تَصْنِيفِ المُحْتَوَى فِي المَادَّةِ التَّاسِعَةِ.
english: There was no objection to the classification of the content in the ninth article.
reason: Natural formal Arabic with an accurate translation.

arabic: نَزَلَ المُتَخَصِّصُ إِلَى العِيَادَةِ وَأَنْقَذَ غُلَامًا بِتَوْفِيقٍ مِنَ اللّهِ.
english: The specialist came down to the clinic and saved a boy with God's help.
reason: Grammatical and plausible; the translation accurately conveys the meaning.

arabic: الوَصِيفُ اِشْتَرَى بِذْلَةً وَرِبْطَةً وَحِذَاءً مُلائِمًا فِي المَدِينَةِ.
english: The young man bought a suit, a tie, and suitable shoes in the city.
reason: الوصيف means a male servant or page, not simply a young man. The Arabic itself describes a plausible purchase.

arabic: تَجَاهَلَ الطَّالِبُ فَشَلَ التَّجْرِبَةِ، وَبَحَثَ عَنِ الحَظِّ فِي هَذَا المَجَالِ.
english: The student ignored the failure of the experiment and looked for luck in this field.
reason: Seeking luck in a field is understandable, and the translation preserves the meaning.

arabic: جَارِي بَلَغَ سَبْعِينَ مِنَ العُمْرِ، وَلَا يَزَالُ الصِّيَامُ يَمْنَحُهُ سُرُورًا.
english: My neighbor has reached seventy years of age, and fasting still gives him pleasure.
reason: A plausible statement with an understood omission of سنة after سبعين; the translation is accurate.

arabic: السِّنْجَابُ قَفَزَ مِنَ الشَّجَرَةِ عِنْدَ ظُهُورِ النَّمِرِ فِي الغَابَةِ.
english: The squirrel jumped from the tree when the tiger appeared in the forest.
reason: A coherent animal scene with correct grammar and translation.

arabic: نَاوَلَتْنِي الجَارَةُ حَفْنَةً مِنَ القَمْحِ وَخَلِيطًا مِنَ الزُّبْدَةِ وَالسُّكَّرِ.
english: The neighbor handed me a handful of wheat and a mixture of butter and sugar.
reason: A plausible exchange of cooking ingredients; the translation is accurate.

arabic: وَجَدَ الغُلَامُ فِي الدُّرْجِ تَأْشِيرَةً، فَتَسَاءَلَ عَنْ عَوْدَةِ بَابَا بَعْدَ بُرْهَةٍ.
english: The boy found a visa in the drawer, so after a moment he wondered about dad's return.
reason: Finding a visa could prompt thoughts about an absent father. بعد برهة can describe when the boy wondered, as translated.

arabic: تَعَلَّمَ الطَّالِبُ فِي الصَّوْتِيَّاتِ أَنَّ الحَلْقَ عُضْوٌ مُعَقَّدٌ جِدًّا.
english: The student learned in phonetics that the throat is a very complex organ.
reason: A plausible textbook statement about phonetics with an accurate translation.

arabic: الرِّجَالُ عَبَدُوا آلِهَةً، ثُمَّ تَحَوَّلُوا بَعْدَ قَرْنٍ وَعَبَدُوا إِلٰهًا وَاحِدًا.
english: The men worshipped gods, then after a century they changed and worshipped one God.
reason: The century-long interval is unusual but possible in a historical collective or fictional context. The translation matches.

arabic: قَرَصَ الغُلَامُ فَخِذِي بِسَبَّابَتِهِ عَبَثًا، فَقَطَبْتُ ثُمَّ صَيَّحْتُ فِي الغُلَامِ.
english: The boy pinched my thigh with his index finger as mischief, so I frowned and then shouted at him.
reason: A plausible scene of mischief and irritation; the index finger can participate in the pinch. The translation conveys the meaning.

arabic: المُهَنْدِسُ اِشْتَغَلَ فِي الجَرَاجِ بِرِعَايَةٍ، ثُمَّ أَلْقَى العَجَلَةَ القَدِيمَةَ.
english: The engineer worked carefully in the garage, then threw away the old wheel.
reason: برعاية means with care or sponsorship in the sense of looking after someone or something; it is unsuitable here for working carefully. بعناية would convey the intended meaning.

arabic: عَادَةً يُشَاهِدُ جَارِي مُسَلْسَلًا سُورِيًّا مُضْحِكًا عَبْرَ شَبَكَةٍ إِلِكْتُرُونِيَّةٍ.
english: Usually my neighbor watches a funny Syrian series over an online network.
reason: A plausible viewing habit. The wording is somewhat formal, and the translation is accurate.

arabic: تَنَاوَلَ الطَّحَّانُ مُبَكِّراً سَنْدَوِيتْشًا وَكَرُوَاسُونًا، ثُمَّ كَنَسَ المَطْحَنَةَ.
english: The miller ate a sandwich and a croissant early, then swept the mill.
reason: Grammatical, plausible, and accurately translated.

arabic: كَانَ الهَمْسْتَرُ جَوْعَانَ، فَتَلَقَّطَ بَاقِيَ الإِجَّاصِ مِنَ الزَّبْدِيَّةِ.
english: The hamster was hungry, so it picked up the rest of the pears from the bowl.
reason: A plausible scene with correct grammar. الإجاص can refer collectively to pears.

arabic: المَنْسَفُ أَكْلِي المُفَضَّلُ، وَأَنَا مُولَعٌ جِدّاً بِالبَهَارِ وَالنَّعْنَاعِ.
english: Mansaf is my favorite food, and I am very fond of spices and mint.
reason: A coherent statement of food preferences with an accurate translation.

arabic: طَلَبَتِ العَزْبَاءُ فِي المَقْهَى مُقَبِّلَاتٍ وَخَضْرَاوَاتٍ وَطَاوُوقاً، ثُمَّ انْتَظَرَتْ.
english: The single woman ordered appetizers, vegetables and tawook at the café, then waited.
reason: The ordering scene is plausible, and the translation matches.

arabic: الجِينْزُ مُتَثَاقِلٌ جِدّاً فِي الصَّيْفِ، فَالجَدَّةُ مَبْسُوطَةٌ بِالجَلَّابِيَّةِ فَقَطْ.
english: Jeans are very heavy in summer, so Grandmother is happy only with the jellabiya.
reason: متثاقل means sluggish or moving laboriously, not physically heavy. It is unsuitable for describing the weight of jeans; ثقيل would fit.

arabic: تَحَرَّكَ الجُرَذُ المَذْعُورُ فِي الزُّقَاقِ المُتَعَرِّجِ، فَوَجَدَ فَضْلَةً فِي القُمَامَةِ.
english: The terrified rat moved through the winding alley and found droppings in the garbage.
reason: Grammatical and plausible. فضلة can denote excrement, although a leftover or scrap is another possible reading.

arabic: أَصْغَى الأَطْفَالُ بِغِبْطَةٍ إِلَى أُسْطُورَةِ العِمْلَاقِ وَتَشْوِيقِهَا فِي الحَفْلَةِ.
english: The children listened joyfully at the party to the legend of the giant and its suspense.
reason: The English follows the Arabic, but coordinating the legend and its suspense as things listened to is an unnatural, forced combination.

arabic: دَافَعَ الجَيْشُ عَنِ الرَّعِيَّةِ بِعِنَادٍ وَمَشَقَّةٍ، وَأَفْشَلَ هُجُومَ العَدُوِّ.
english: The army defended the people with stubbornness and hardship, and thwarted the enemy's attack.
reason: Slightly formal phrasing, but the military scene is coherent and accurately translated.

arabic: دَمْدَمَ الطِّفْلُ المُفْحَمُ مِنْ غَرَابَةِ هَذَا اللُّغْزِ، وَلَمْ يَجِدْ جَوَاباً.
english: The silenced child muttered at the strangeness of this riddle, and found no answer.
reason: A child left speechless by a puzzling riddle can subsequently mutter. The translation is acceptable.

arabic: فِي الكَاتِدْرَائِيِّ سَالَ الزَّيْتُ مِنَ القِنْدِيلِ وَغَمَرَ الطَّاقَ.
english: In the cathedral, oil ran from the lamp and flooded the arch.
reason: الكاتدرائي is an adjectival form, not the noun 'cathedral'; the expected noun is الكاتدرائية.

arabic: الخَجَلُ لَيْسَ عَيْباً فِي المَدْرَسَةِ، لَكِنَّ القَمْعَ وَاللَّامُبَالَاةَ عَيْبٌ فَظِيعٌ.
english: Shyness is not a defect at school, but repression and indifference are a terrible flaw.
reason: Grammatical and coherent. The singular predicate عيب can characterize repression and indifference together as one flaw.

arabic: الجَدَّةُ صَبُورٌ دَائِماً، وَلِسَانُهَا مُؤَنِّبٌ لَكِنَّهُ مُهَدِّئٌ لِلأَطْفَالِ.
english: Grandmother is always patient, and her tongue is reproachful but calming to the children.
reason: صبور correctly applies to a woman. The figurative description of her tongue as reproachful yet calming is plausible and accurately translated.
